title: The Glenrowan Line
style: folk, traditional Australian bush ballad, moderate tempo, acoustic guitar, fiddle, upright bass, snare drum, acoustic, steady, somber, ballad
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The morning mist lay thick and cold upon the Glenrowan line
The plough-steel plates upon my chest
A heavy
Grim design
My brothers trapped within the inn
Their powder burned and gone
I stood alone beneath the gums to face the bitter dawn

[Verse 2]
With heavy breath and battered helm
I stepped into the gray
My hand upon my pistol grip
The final card to play
The troopers stared in disbelief at a ghost in iron clad
The last man of the Kelly gang
A broken
Bleeding lad

[Chorus]
And the sergeant roared with a trembling voice
"Keep the townsfolk at bay
Hold the line and stand your ground
Let none approach this way"
They watched me from the railway track
A hundred silent eyes
As I stood my ground for a final time beneath the winter skies

[Verse 3]
They poured their lead upon my chest
It sparked and ricocheted
But I kept my hand upon my hip
Defiant and unswayed
I taunted them to do their worst
My voice an iron bell
A wild colonial Irish son walking through the gates of Hell

[Verse 4]
But a man is flesh beneath the steel
No matter how he's willed
And the rifles echoed from the scrub across the muddy field
Sergeant Steele took aim below the plates where the iron didn't shield
And brought the last bushranger crashing to the yield

[Chorus]
While the sergeant roared with a trembling voice
"Keep the townsfolk at bay
Hold the line and stand your ground
Let none approach this way"
They watched me from the railway track
A hundred silent eyes
As I stood my ground for a final time beneath the winter skies
